item.title: Army women make history with 30–1 win over Police in Sukuna Bowl basketball
item.description: The Army women's team has made history in the Vodafone 2026 Ratu Sukuna Bowl Basketball Tournament, defeating Police 30–1 in the first women's basketball match in 15 years, while the Police men's team beat Army 34-15.

item.title: Police aim for ninth straight Sukuna Bowl football victory
item.description: The Fiji Police football team is confident of retaining the Sukuna Bowl football trophy for the ninth consecutive year when it faces the Republic of Fiji Military Forces team today. Assistant Superintendent of Police Sanjay Chand, who is also the team manager, says the team has been preparing well and has been in camp since last week.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Police football team is confident of retaining the Sukuna Bowl football trophy for the ninth consecutive year when it faces the Republic of Fiji Military Forces team today.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Sanjay Chand, who is also the team manager, says the team has been preparing well and has been in camp since last week.

Chand says the team was at the Fiji Football Association yesterday for its final preparations ahead of the much-anticipated clash.

He says the Police team has held the trophy for the past eight years and is determined to continue its winning record this year.

Chand says the team has been focusing on strengthening its attacking force, with the aim of scoring early and bringing more players forward.

He knows that the RFMF team will be a strong opponent, as they have been in camp for more than two months.

However, Chand says Police also has a strong squad, with talented players selected from districts across the country following the recent Police Inter-District Tournament.

He is calling on Police supporters and the families of the players to turn out in full support, saying their encouragement is important to the team.

The Police team for tomorrow's match includes Ilaisa Nayasi of Labasa FC, Ilisoni Lolaivalu of Ba FC, Sitiveni Rakai and Madhwan Gounder of Rewa FC, Ratu Dau, Alvin Chand of Nasinu FC, Rumeru Tekiate of Suva FC, Iliesa Lino and Jitoko Vulava of Labasa FC, Joeli Ranitu of Tailevu/Naitasiri FC and Semi Matalau of Rewa FC.

The match will kick off at 10am today at Buckhurst Park.

item.title: Basketball returns to Sukuna Bowl after 15-year break
item.description: The last time basketball featured in the Sukuna Bowl was in 2011, and the much-anticipated return will see the two forces go head-to-head tomorrow. Fiji Police Basketball Manager, Acting Inspector Voniani Namua says the team is currently camping at Nabua Secondary School as part of its preparations.
item.content:encoded:
The last time basketball featured in the Sukuna Bowl was in 2011, and the much-anticipated return will see the two forces go head-to-head tomorrow.

Fiji Police Basketball Manager, Acting Inspector Voniani Namua says the team is currently camping at Nabua Secondary School as part of its preparations.

Namua says he has been meeting with the RFMF basketball management over the past few days, and both sides have been working closely together ahead of the competition.

He says they have developed a good relationship with their RFMF counterparts and are looking forward to an enjoyable match.

Namua says winning is not the main focus for the Police team, as the competition is also an opportunity to continue promoting this year's Sukuna Bowl theme, “Drug Free Fiji: Our Goal, One Mission.”

He also confirms that both forces have agreed that no civilian players will take part in this year's basketball competition, with the teams made up of their respective personnel.

Namua has thanked Vodafone, the major sponsor, and all other sponsors for their support towards the 2026 Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl.

He is also encouraging families and members of the public to come out and support the basketball teams tomorrow and on the 20th.

The women's basketball game will start at 9am tomorrow, followed by the men's game at 11am at the FMF Gymnasium.

item.title: Salabiau earns All Blacks Sevens call-up after impressive NPC season
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 18/11/2026 Fiji-born Waikato winger Waisake Salabiau has been named in the 22-member All Blacks Sevens squad for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS World 7s Series.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 18/11/2026

Fiji-born Waikato winger Waisake Salabiau has been named in the 22-member All Blacks Sevens squad for the 2026/27 HSBC SVNS World 7s Series.

Salabiau had a breakout season for Waikato, showcasing his speed and footwork as he scored seven tries in nine NPC matches.

He will be joined by Akuila Rokolisoa and Kele Lasaqa.

Head coach Willie Rickards has named five uncapped players for this season, including Salabiau, Brayden Neilson, Grady Forbes, Nathan Salmon and Adam Morrison.

Rickards has also recalled experienced playmakers Joe Webber and Andrew Knewstubb after both players missed the 2026 sevens season.

Rob Rush and experienced campaigner Sione Molia will co-captain the All Blacks Sevens side.

The All Blacks will open their Dubai 7s campaign against the Fiji Airways Fiji men's national 7s side at 8.36pm next Saturday.

They will then face Spain at 11.39pm before meeting France at 4.22am on Sunday, 29th November.

The men's cup semi-finals will kick off at 10.06pm on Sunday, with the final scheduled for 4.11am on Monday, 30th November.
